checks.statement: A loading indicator may appear inside a button while its action is in progress.
checks.condition: When a button action takes a few seconds.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Placement: A loading indicator may appear inside a button while its action is in progress.

evidence.result: The cited specimen is a standalone web example; it contains no application screen/navigation policy that can enforce this condition: “When a button action takes a few seconds.”.

implementation.notes: The condition is “When a button action takes a few seconds.” and the instruction is “A loading indicator may appear inside a button while its action is in progress.”. This is an app-level content, layout, or product-selection decision; the standalone reusable control/specimen does not have the surrounding screen context needed to apply it. This disposition covers this exact condition only.

checks.statement: Do not transition a loading indicator into a determinate progress indicator; when progress changes from unknown to known, transition between indeterminate and determinate progress indicators instead.
checks.condition: When progress becomes measurable.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Usage: Do not transition a loading indicator into a determinate progress indicator; when progress changes from unknow

evidence.result: The loading specimen is separate from the progress specimen and does not transition either component or content between them.

implementation.notes: The check applies when a single process changes from unknown to known progress. The baseline has no process controller that transitions this indicator, so the component cannot violate or perform that transition.

checks.statement: Expose a progressbar role and an accessible label that explains the operation and affected content.
checks.condition: When exposing a loading indicator to assistive technology.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Labeling elements: Expose a progressbar role and an accessible label that explains the operation and affected content.

evidence.result: The rendered path calls ProgressAttributes(), which adds role=progressbar and aria-label="Loading"; however the label is fixed and does not identify the affected content for a concrete operation.

implementation.notes: The role and an accessible name are present, correcting the earlier false absence claim. The remaining ambiguity is whether a generic “Loading” label is sufficient for this context-free specimen; the helper provides no operation/content-specific name.

checks.statement: Keep the indicator between 24dp and 240dp, preserve the container-to-active-indicator ratio, and scale it with larger panes without exceeding 240dp.
checks.condition: When sizing by placement and breakpoint.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Responsive layout: Keep the indicator between 24dp and 240dp, preserve the container-to-active-indicator ratio, and scale it with

evidence.result: Reproduction: inspect default contained and uncontained previews. Both containers render 48×48 CSS px with a 38×38 active indicator, within the stated range. The implementation keeps those fixed token dimensions at larger panes and has no responsive scale-up path.

implementation.notes: The exposed default dimensions satisfy the 24dp–240dp bound and preserve the 38/48 relationship; the unmet part is scaling the indicator with larger panes. This is not marked missing because an arbitrary-token clamp is absent.

checks.statement: For the contained style, use on-primary-container for the active indicator and primary-container for its container.
checks.condition: When styling a contained loading indicator.

sourceHistory.summary: Captured the specific Contained rule: For the contained style, use on-primary-container for the active indicator and primary-container for its conta

evidence.result: The mapper accepts base and contained active-indicator color plus contained container color and scopes contained tokens to data-variant=contained; CSS applies container and currentColor to the shape.

implementation.notes: The contained style consumes separately mapped active/container colors through the contained variant selector.

checks.statement: Default and contained loading indicators are M3 Expressive configurations.
checks.condition: When exposing loading indicator configuration availability.

sourceHistory.summary: Captured the specific Configurations rule: Default and contained loading indicators are M3 Expressive configurations.

evidence.result: The component mapper has a contained variant selector and the CSS explicitly makes the uncontained variant transparent.

implementation.notes: The web component exposes uncontained and contained visual variants through token mapping and variant selector.

checks.statement: Use primary for the active indicator in the default, uncontained style.
checks.condition: When styling an uncontained loading indicator.

sourceHistory.summary: Captured the specific Default rule: Use primary for the active indicator in the default, uncontained style.

evidence.result: The default active-indicator color maps to `--_loading-color` and drives the shape’s currentColor; the uncontained variant makes only the background transparent.

implementation.notes: The default indicator color is applied independently of container fill; the exact primary role value is supplied by source tokens.

checks.statement: The default loading indicator size is 48dp and its shape container is 38dp.
checks.condition: When using the default loading indicator size.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured Measurements prose or table: The default loading indicator size is 48dp and its shape container is 38dp.

evidence.result: The actual rendered uncontained and contained indicators are 48×48 CSS px with a 38×38 active shape, matching the configured default container/indicator dimensions.

implementation.notes: The initial assessment reversed the active and container measurements; the observed geometry confirms a 48px container around a 38px active indicator.

checks.statement: Scale the default 48dp indicator upward on larger windows so it remains proportional to surrounding empty space, without exceeding 240dp.
checks.condition: When a loading indicator appears in a larger pane or window.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated the explicit Larger windows instruction: Scale the default 48dp indicator upward on larger windows so it remains proportional to surrounding empty spac

evidence.result: At the default page size both variants remain 48×48 CSS px; the stylesheet has no viewport or available-pane observer/media rule that scales the default indicator upward on larger windows.

implementation.notes: The source explicitly requires proportional scale-up on larger windows. The implementation retains fixed default token dimensions, so the large-window behavior is absent; this is independent of the 240dp bound.

checks.statement: Maintain at least 3:1 contrast between the active indicator and its background or containing component.
checks.condition: When selecting indicator colors.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from Interaction & style: Maintain at least 3:1 contrast between the active indicator and its background or containing component.

evidence.result: The active indicator and background use tokenized colors, but no source rule computes or guards contrast between them.

implementation.notes: The 3:1 requirement depends on the resolved theme tokens and surface behind the indicator; the code does not enforce it and a computed-style contrast check is needed.
